style_exemplars.notes: hull presented dry at the waterline with black boot-topping, no water; low three-quarter bow view; shadow even subtler than aircraft exemplar

style_exemplars.subject: Hughes YAH-64 prototype, US Army, real museum-style studio photograph
style_exemplars.notes: backdrop reads slightly warmer gray than the renders - acceptable range; MAIN ROTOR BLADES MAY RUN PAST THE FRAME EDGES, fuselage fully framed is the rule; visible floor-to-wall studio falloff acceptable

exemplar_selection_rule: pass the exemplar matching the machine's category (aircraft/warship/helicopter); for tanks and vehicles (no exemplar yet) use the aircraft exemplar for tone plus the JSON contract
purpose: Style contract for every DvsU unit image. Send this JSON + the style exemplar image + the machine's verified historical reference photo to GPT Image 2. JSON controls STYLE; the reference photo controls IDENTITY/ACCURACY; the machine brief controls configuration.

subject.count: exactly one machine, the specific named variant from the Graphics List brief
subject.placement: centered, hull/fuselage fully in frame; exception: helicopter main-rotor blades may extend past the frame edges (see helicopter exemplar)
subject.pose: static, wheels/hull grounded as if parked in a studio; landing gear down for aircraft on the ground

camera.angle: three-quarter front view, from the machine's front-left or front-right
camera.elevation: slightly elevated, roughly 20-30 degrees above the horizon line
camera.lens: medium telephoto look (~85-135mm equivalent), minimal perspective distortion, everything in sharp focus

background.type: seamless white studio cyclorama, no visible horizon seam
background.tone: clean near-white with a barely perceptible cool gray falloff toward edges, never pure clipped #FFFFFF everywhere
background.elements: nothing else: no sky, no terrain, no hangar, no props

ground_and_shadow.surface: implied white studio floor, same tone as background
ground_and_shadow.shadow: single soft contact shadow directly beneath the machine, tight spread, low opacity, softly diffused edges
ground_and_shadow.reflections: none or barely perceptible; matte floor, not glossy showroom

lighting.scheme: high-key soft studio lighting, large overhead softbox feel
lighting.speculars: controlled soft highlights on metal surfaces, no blown hotspots

rendering.style: photorealistic, museum-grade product photography of the real machine
rendering.detail: visible panel lines, rivets, fasteners, canopy framing; crisp identifying details
rendering.wear: light, historically plausible surface variation; not factory-CGI-clean, not battle-damaged

markings.rule: only historically accurate insignia, codes, and stencils for the exact variant, operator, and year in the brief
markings.monetization_rule: German WWII machines carry the Balkenkreuz, never the swastika

exclusions: no stands, jacks, cradles, or display mounts
no text overlays, watermarks, captions, or logos added to the image
no weapons-impact damage, casualties, or combat scene elements
no second machine, vehicles, or background props

per_machine_slots.designation: full designation and variant, e.g. 'Boeing B-17G Flying Fortress'
per_machine_slots.configuration_year: year or configuration state to depict
per_machine_slots.operator: nation + service branch for correct markings
per_machine_slots.error_prone_details: engine count, prop/rotor config, turret shapes, canopy style, era-correct equipment for THIS variant
per_machine_slots.reference_photo: verified historical reference image (Wikimedia static_reference_cache), passed as an input image alongside the style exemplar
